threat_event: Attacker signs in to the remote-desktop service and uses the agent on the city hall BAS engineering workstation to change setpoints, schedules, or programs in the city BAS
threat_source: Cybercriminal or hacktivist group targeting building systems (credential stuffing or phishing)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Agent allowed unattended access with a password-only account and bypassed the city VPN; never disclosed to the city IT manager; session log never reviewed; the workstation reaches the supervisory controller through the shared administrator account
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, AC-17)
existing_controls: MFA turned on and unattended access turned off 2026-08-18; disclosed to the city IT manager 2026-08-21
treatment_plan: Remove the agent and cancel the subscription; use only the city VPN with city MFA for after-hours alarm response; review the session log weekly until removal (POAM-001)

threat_event: Someone who knows the shared BAS supervisory administrator password (the previous integrator's staff, or anyone who sees the phone's notes) changes the city BAS or locks the owner and the city out
threat_source: Former integrator staff or an opportunistic outsider
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One shared built-in administrator account; password set in 2023 and never changed; stored in the phone's notes app; no named accounts; BAS audit log never reviewed
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-08 BAS supervisory controller and 31 field controllers (BP-01)
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, IA-5)
existing_controls: Supervisory controller reachable only from the city network (city VPN or on site)
treatment_plan: Move the password into a password manager now; ask the city in writing to change it and to create a named administrator account for the owner; review the BAS audit log monthly (POAM-002)

threat_event: Phishing or session theft takes over the owner's productivity suite account and exposes drawings, cardholder exports, CUI, and alarm emails
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: The suite holds most customer data in one folder tree; alarm emails and contract notices arrive there; no review of sign-in history
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, IA-2(1)); CT-F FAR 52.204-21(b)(1)(vi)
existing_controls: MFA with an authenticator app; provider phishing filtering
treatment_plan: Monthly sign-in review; phishing-resistant sign-in method when the provider offers it on the plan; recovery codes in the sealed envelope

threat_event: Malware or ransomware on the laptop steals stored customer data and uses the city VPN session to reach the BAS network
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Daily work under an administrator account; laptop shares a flat home network with family devices; built-in antivirus only
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, AC-6); CT-F FAR 52.204-21(b)(1)(ii)
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; automatic updates; built-in antivirus; VPN requires city MFA
treatment_plan: Standard account for daily work (POAM-003); separate work network (R-012); no ransom payment for the city's systems (Fla. Stat. 282.3186 binds the city)

threat_event: Laptop failure, theft, or ransomware destroys the only copies of controller programs and door schedule exports, so a failed controller cannot be restored within the RTO
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Engineering folder excluded from cloud sync; no backup; 4 of 11 library copies already older than the running program (P07)
affected_asset_or_process: Controller programs and door schedules (BP-01, BP-02)
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, CP-9)
existing_controls: Field controllers keep running their last programs; door controllers cache schedules
treatment_plan: Save each running program after every change; nightly cloud backup of the engineering folder plus an encrypted external drive; quarterly comparison test (POAM-004)

threat_event: The owner is suddenly unavailable (illness, injury, or travel) and nobody can answer city alarms, remove badges, or change schedules
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One person holds every role and every credential; the city has no backup technician; no manual operation sheets; no sealed emergency access
affected_asset_or_process: All processes, most of all BP-01 and BP-02
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, CP-2)
existing_controls: City IT manager is the second access control administrator; controllers keep running
treatment_plan: City-approved backup controls firm with a credential hand-over process; manual operation sheet per building; sealed emergency access envelope with the owner's attorney; account list to the city IT manager

threat_event: The owner loses the phone or it fails, locking the owner out of every MFA-protected account while alarms are going to that phone
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Every MFA prompt and the access control app on one personal phone; no recovery codes stored anywhere
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, IA-5)
existing_controls: Phone passcode, encryption, and remote wipe
treatment_plan: Recovery codes and a second authenticator method; sealed envelope (POL-01 7.6)

threat_event: GSA drawings marked CUI are disclosed through an open sharing link, a misdirected email, or a lost device
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: CUI in the general cloud folder and email; "anyone with the link" default (fixed 2026-08-12); no marking routine; no CUI training
existing_controls: Paper sets locked in the van cabinet; laptop encrypted; open link disabled and reported to the prime 2026-08-12
treatment_plan: Restricted CUI folder, not synced to the phone; delete other copies; mark excerpts; CUI training (POAM-005)

threat_event: City cardholder exports (312 cardholders with credential numbers and access history) are exposed from the laptop or cloud storage
threat_source: Owner error, laptop theft, or account takeover
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 21 monthly exports kept although only the latest is needed; exports in the general folder
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(2) and (6)(a); CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, SI-12)
treatment_plan: Keep the two latest exports only; city records folder; delete the rest and confirm to the city

threat_event: A notice deadline is missed after an incident (city 24 hours, prime immediately, FAR 1 or 3 business days, Florida 10 days)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No written plan or contact list before 2026-09-04; clocks differ by contract and start at different events; no cyber insurance or outside responder
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, IR-6); C-GOVERNMENT-R01 (BTTRG 1.6.1); CT-F FAR 52.204-25(d)
existing_controls: Owner reported the CUI link to the prime the same day it was found
treatment_plan: Adopt the P08 runbook and printed contact sheet; walk it through; cyber insurance quotes that include breach response (POAM-007)

threat_event: A part the owner supplies for the federal building is covered telecommunications equipment, a Kaspersky product, or subject to a FASCSA order, and goes unreported
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No screening against FAR 52.204-23, 52.204-25, or 52.204-30; some parts bought on online marketplaces; one switch with an unconfirmed manufacturer (P07)
existing_controls: Most parts from the authorized controls distributor
treatment_plan: Confirm or replace the switch; parts check and SAM.gov "FASCSA order" search before every federal building purchase; distributor-only purchasing (POAM-008)

threat_event: An attacker or an infected family device on the home network reaches the laptop or changes the router
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Default router administrator password; firmware never updated; one Wi-Fi network for work and family
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, SC-7); CT-F FAR 52.204-21(b)(1)(x)
existing_controls: Laptop firewall; TLS and VPN for all work traffic
treatment_plan: Owner-owned router with a separate work network; unique administrator password; quarterly firmware check

threat_event: Exempt city building information (BAS point lists, a library door schedule excerpt) kept or reused by a consumer AI chatbot provider
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Chatbot used June to August 2026 with the model-improvement setting on; no approved-tools rule
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 119.071(3)(a) and (b)4.; CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, SA-9)
existing_controls: Setting turned off and chat history deleted 2026-08-12; reported to the city IT manager 2026-08-13
treatment_plan: No customer data in any AI tool (POL-01 9.6); use the chatbot only for general questions (P10 AI-002)

threat_event: The owner configures the access control vendor's face verification add-on at the city hall staff entrance without an assessment, and it wrongly rejects some staff more than others, exposes face data, or creates templates the city cannot protect from disclosure
threat_source: Owner and customer decision (configuring a third-party AI feature)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor trial on in the city's tenant; the city facilities manager asked the owner to configure it; no assessment, consent, retention terms, or counsel view
affected_asset_or_process: City access control tenant (BP-02); city hall staff
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171 and 501.702 (biometric data); Fla. Stat. 119.071; CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, RA-3)
existing_controls: No staff enrolled; the owner has not configured the add-on
treatment_plan: Do not configure the add-on unless the conditions in P10 are met and the city decides in writing (P10 AI-001)

threat_event: A hurricane closes the home office and city buildings and cuts power and internet for several days
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Home office and all customer buildings in the same Florida metro area
regulatory_driver: CT-C security exhibit (SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Moderate, CP-2)
existing_controls: SaaS reachable over the phone hotspot; the laptop goes with the owner; city has its own storm plan for its buildings
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low. Before a storm, save all running controller programs (R-005) and charge the laptop and hotspot
